newsitem.title: USA: HFS adding PHH Corp. in $1.7 billion deal.
newsitem.headline: HFS adding PHH Corp. in $1.7 billion deal.

text.p: HFS Inc., the hotel and real estate franchisor, said Monday it would acquire PHH Corp., a provider of corporate relocation and other financial services, in a stock deal worth $1.7 billion.

The transaction values PHH at $49.50 a share, and following the news, PHH's stock soared $17.625 to $48.375 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange. HFS was up $1.625 at $75.75, also on the NYSE.
HFS, which also owns the Avis Corp. car rental firm, said it would issue 23.2 million shares in exchange for PHH's 34.8 million common shares.
Based in Hunt Valley, Md., PHH handles car leasing, real estate and insurance services for 3,000 corporate and government clients that relocate their employees.
PHH, which has annual revenues of $600 million and earnings of $86 million, operates in the United States, Canada and Europe.

"PHH is a perfect strategic fit within HFS and represents our continued evolution into a global service provider for consumers, corporations and other organisations," said Henry Silverman, chairman and chief executive officer of Parsippany, N.J.-based HFS.

"In corporate relocation, our existing business combined with PHH's relocation and other real estate services will benefit the transferring employees of our corporate customers as well as our franchised real estate brokers," he said.
Silverman also said that PHH's fleet leasing will boost HFS's fleet business and its Avis rental car operations.
HFS said it will take a one-time charge as a result of the acquisition, which is expected to be completed in the first quarter next year.
The company said it has not yet estimated the amount of the charge.
PHH Chief Executive Robert Kunisch will join the HFS board of directors when the deal is completed.
